scope: NetShield research prototype: Python application, runtime and development requirements, both Dockerfiles, the Go capture prototype, the built serving image netshield:ci, and the repository working tree.

findings.title: lightgbm 4.5.0 had a known high-severity vulnerability
findings.evidence: CVE-2024-43598 was reported for 4.5.0. requirements.txt now pins lightgbm==4.7.0; the serving image does not install lightgbm at all.
findings.impact: Training-only dependency; it was never on the serving path.
findings.remediation: Upgraded to 4.7.0 and re-ran the full test suite (77 passed).

findings.title: python-socketio 5.11.2 had known vulnerabilities
findings.evidence: CVE-2026-48804 (fixed 5.16.2) and CVE-2025-61765 (fixed 5.14.0). requirements now pin python-socketio==5.16.2.
findings.impact: Socket.IO is on the live-alert path.
findings.remediation: Upgraded to 5.16.2 and re-ran the full test suite.

findings.title: eventlet 0.36.1 had a known vulnerability
findings.evidence: CVE-2025-58068, fixed 0.40.3. Both requirements files pin eventlet==0.40.3.
findings.impact: eventlet was the configured async worker class.
findings.remediation: Upgraded to 0.40.3 and re-ran the full test suite.

findings.title: requests 2.32.0 had known vulnerabilities
findings.evidence: CVE-2024-47081 (fixed 2.32.4) and CVE-2026-25645 (fixed 2.33.0). Both requirements files pin requests==2.33.0.
findings.impact: Used for the optional AbuseIPDB enrichment call.
findings.remediation: Upgraded to 2.33.0 and re-ran the full test suite.

findings.title: Development collector still installs scapy 2.5.0
findings.evidence: GHSA-cq46-m9x9-j8w2 affects scapy session-file loading. pyflowmeter 0.2.4 pins scapy==2.5.0. The serving image does not install pyflowmeter and uses scapy==2.7.0, which reports zero Python findings.
findings.impact: The advisory requires a local user to load a malicious .pkl.gz Scapy session with -s. NetShield never calls the session loader and never accepts session files. The serving artifact is not affected.
findings.remediation: The runtime image is fixed. The development collector remains on 2.5.0 because of the upstream pin; replace or vendor pyflowmeter before shipping a collector built on this environment.
findings.target: accepted for the research collector; revisit when pyflowmeter updates

findings.title: pytest had a known vulnerability and was installed in the serving image
findings.evidence: PYSEC-2026-1845, fixed 9.0.3. The runtime/development split now keeps pytest out of requirements-runtime.txt, and requirements.txt pins pytest==9.0.3.
findings.impact: Test tooling was previously part of the image attack surface.
findings.remediation: Split runtime and development requirements; upgraded pytest; image Python findings are now zero.

findings.title: python-dotenv 1.0.0 had a known vulnerability
findings.evidence: CVE-2026-28684, fixed 1.2.2. Both requirements files pin python-dotenv==1.2.2.
findings.impact: Used for local environment loading.
findings.remediation: Upgraded to 1.2.2 and re-ran the full test suite.

findings.title: Flask 2.3.2 / Werkzeug 2.3.8 had known advisories
findings.evidence: Flask now 3.1.3 and Werkzeug >=3.1.9,<4. pip-audit reports zero findings for requirements-runtime.txt.
findings.impact: Core web framework.
findings.remediation: Coordinated major upgrade; full test suite passes.

findings.title: Dockerfile.capture had no HEALTHCHECK
findings.evidence: Dockerfile.capture now defines a pgrep-based HEALTHCHECK.
findings.impact: A hung capture process is now visible to an orchestrator.
findings.remediation: Added the health probe and rebuilt the capture image successfully.

findings.title: Go capture prototype pinned an old golang.org/x/sys
findings.evidence: golang.org/x/sys moved from a 2019 pseudo-version to v0.50.0; go.mod now requires Go 1.26; the builder image was bumped to golang:1.26-alpine. Trivy reports zero Go vulnerabilities and go test passes.
findings.impact: The Go capture program is a prototype and is not on the Python serving path.
findings.remediation: Updated the dependency and builder image, rebuilt netshield-capture:ci, and re-ran the Go tests.

findings.title: Container image vulnerability scan was not performed
findings.evidence: netshield:ci was built and scanned with Trivy 0.76.1: 0 CRITICAL, 47 HIGH, 74 MEDIUM, 65 LOW; all 186 are unfixed Debian 13.7 OS packages; 0 Python findings; 0 secrets; 0 misconfigurations. docs/security_gate.json passes.
findings.impact: The remaining OS findings are inherited from the official python:3.11-slim base image. None has a fixed version in the Debian archive as of the scan date.
findings.remediation: Keep the scan in CI, rebuild on base-image updates, and track the accepted OS baseline in docs/SECURITY_AND_COMPLIANCE.md. Replacing the base image was evaluated and did not reduce the count: python:3.13-slim-trixie had 197 findings and distroless python3-debian12 had 330 including 2 CRITICAL.
findings.target: scan resolved; baseline reviewed on every base-image refresh

findings.title: External penetration test not commissioned
findings.evidence: No third-party test has been performed. The assistant cannot commission or complete one. An internal automated assessment (OWASP ZAP baseline and Bandit) was performed and is not a substitute.
findings.impact: No independent assurance for authentication, authorization, tenancy isolation, upload parsing, or the deployment boundary.
findings.remediation: Engage an independent tester using docs/PENETRATION_TEST_PLAN.md; resolve critical/high findings and retest.

findings.title: Secrets are supplied through environment variables, not a managed secret store
findings.evidence: SECRET_KEY, LIVE_CAPTURE_API_KEY, NETSHIELD_ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH, NETSHIELD_PROXY_SHARED_SECRET, MODEL_SIGNING_KEY, ABUSEIPDB_API_KEY are read from the environment.
findings.impact: Environment variables can leak through process listings, crash dumps, orchestration config, and CI logs. There is no rotation or audit trail.
findings.remediation: Use a managed secret manager or KMS/HSM, scope secrets per environment, rotate them, and document the rotation runbook.

findings.title: Retention and deletion do not cover backups, object storage, or enrichment caches
findings.evidence: docs/PRIVACY_AND_DATA_LIFECYCLE.md and docs/PRODUCT_BOUNDARY_AND_THREAT_MODEL.md: tenant purge and tenant deletion cover database rows only.
findings.impact: Deleted flow metadata can survive in backups or third-party caches, which breaks a deletion promise.
findings.remediation: Define backup retention and restore-deletion procedures; document the enrichment cache TTL; add a deletion verification test.

findings.title: Application audit log is not tamper-evident
findings.evidence: Audit events are an append-only database table, but there is no hash chain, WORM storage, or independent monitoring.
findings.impact: A privileged database operator could alter or delete audit history without detection.
findings.remediation: Add hash-chaining and export to append-only storage; alert on audit write failures.

findings.title: Security scans were documented but not enforced in CI
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/security.yml runs tests, the secret scan, the registry gate, a runtime dependency audit, an image build, a Trivy scan, and scripts/security_gate.py. The gate fails on critical findings, fixable findings, secrets, and failed misconfigurations.
findings.impact: Findings can no longer regress silently once the workflow is enabled on the repository host.
findings.remediation: Added the workflow and the gate with unit tests.

findings.title: The local virtual environment contains dev-only packages with advisories
findings.evidence: The environment includes training and documentation packages that are not declared runtime dependencies. The runtime requirement audit reports 0 vulnerabilities in 51 packages.
findings.impact: The local environment is not the production image. Reporting the environment count as the product's exposure would be misleading.
findings.remediation: Track requirements-runtime.txt as the shipped exposure and keep the environment scan for developer hygiene.

findings.title: The serving image could not boot because app.py imports training modules excluded by .dockerignore
findings.evidence: The first rebuilt image failed with ModuleNotFoundError for training and training.preprocessor. app.py imports training.model_registry and joblib unpickles classes from training.preprocessor.
findings.impact: A previously published image would have failed its health check and served nothing. The bug was invisible to source-level tests because they run from the repository root.
findings.remediation: .dockerignore now keeps exactly training/__init__.py, training/model_registry.py, and training/preprocessor.py. The rebuilt image boots and returns 200 on /healthz, /readyz, /, and /research with a read-only root filesystem.

findings.title: Debian 13.7 base image has 186 unfixed OS package advisories
findings.evidence: Trivy: 47 HIGH, 74 MEDIUM, 65 LOW, 0 CRITICAL, 0 with a fixed version. The packages are util-linux, ncurses, perl-base, libsqlite3, systemd libraries, and similar base packages. Base-image alternatives were measured: python:3.13-slim-trixie 197, distroless python3-debian12 330 (2 CRITICAL).
findings.impact: The application does not expose most of these packages to network input, but a compromised container could use them for local privilege escalation. The base image cannot be patched from the repository today.
findings.remediation: Accepted baseline risk with compensating controls: non-root user, read-only root filesystem in Compose, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, a local-demo bind address, minimal runtime dependencies, and a gate that fails on CRITICAL or fixable findings. Refresh the base image on a schedule and re-scan.
findings.target: review every base-image refresh and before any pilot

findings.title: Compose deployment did not harden the container
findings.evidence: docker-compose.yml previously ran with default capabilities and a writable root filesystem.
findings.impact: A compromised process had more privileges and persistence paths than necessary.
findings.remediation: Added read_only, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, tmpfs /tmp, and named volumes for the only writable application paths. Verified the image boots and serves 200 responses under those settings.

findings.title: Bandit reported a possible SQL-injection vector and unsafe random use
findings.evidence: B608 on DDL/DML built from hardcoded internal names; B311 on demo-fixture randomness. Neither accepted request data.
findings.impact: No exploitable path was found, but unexplained findings hide real ones.
findings.remediation: Documented each site with a targeted nosec justification and a comment explaining why the value is trusted. Bandit now reports 0 HIGH and 0 MEDIUM; 5 LOW findings remain in development-only scripts.

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy allows inline styles
findings.evidence: OWASP ZAP baseline reports CSP style-src unsafe-inline. The UI uses inline style attributes and one inline style block. Inline scripts are not allowed and Jinja autoescaping is enabled.
findings.impact: An HTML-injection flaw could inject style rules and exfiltrate data through CSS selectors. No inline script execution is possible.
findings.remediation: Move the remaining inline styles into stylesheets, then remove unsafe-inline. Tracked as a UI refactor.

enterprise_readiness.reason: No external penetration test has been completed. Open medium findings remain for secret management, retention/deletion coverage, and audit tamper-evidence. The Debian base image carries 186 unfixed OS advisories that are accepted as baseline risk with compensating controls. Critical findings are zero and the serving image has zero fixable findings, but that is not the same as an assurance opinion.
